"North Korea continues streak of weapons tests with multiple ballistic missile launches"
(CBS copy reads as AP-sourced wire text.)

North Korea on Monday fired multiple ballistic missiles toward its eastern waters, South Korea's military said, "adding to a recent streak of weapons demonstrations that has heightened tensions during a prolonged freeze in diplomacy."
South Korea's Joint Chiefs of Staff said the missiles were fired from an area around Pyongyang, "where the country has used its airport as a major launch site in recent years." The JCS did not immediately specify how many missiles they detected or how far they flew.
Japan's Defense Ministry said it detected AT LEAST TWO missiles and assessed they landed in waters outside Japan's exclusive economic zone.
"The launch came days after South Korea on FRIDAY flight-tested its first domestically developed hypersonic weapon, designed to fly at least five times the speed of sound and evade missile defense systems, which President Lee Jae Myung described as an important step in strengthening the South's conventional defense capabilities."
Includes the 3 Oct hypersonic intermediate-range missile test, other missile tests, live-fire drills, and the commissioning of a new warship.
"Tensions were further worsened after three South Korean soldiers were injured in land mine explosions LAST MONTH near the heavily armed inter-Korean border. The South's military and the U.S.-led United Nations Command concluded the blasts were caused by devices planted by North Korea, which has denied responsibility and ridiculed the South's demands for an apology."
Kim has halted all diplomacy and cooperation with South Korea and described the neighbour as a permanent enemy. He has rebuffed Trump's calls to revive diplomacy (broken down 2019); his government demands Washington abandon its "hostile" policy and drop denuclearisation as a precondition.
"Lee has also called for strengthening South Korea's conventional defense capabilities while reducing its reliance on the United States. Washington unilaterally decided to scale back a major military exercise with South Korea in August, with Mr. Trump citing his 'very good relationship' with Kim."

CONFLICT WITH AL JAZEERA: CBS says the South Korean hypersonic test was FRIDAY and the DMZ mine blast LAST MONTH; Al Jazeera says THURSDAY and LAST WEEK. Trust CBS/AP on the mine blast timing ("last month" matches earlier reporting); the hypersonic test day is unresolved - write around it ("in recent days").
